criteria.text: Given a new request, when it is logged, then the system tracks its lifecycle stages.
Given a request update, when it is processed, then the system updates the status and history.
Trust: The system maintains an audit trail of status changes.

stories.notes: Adds a lifecycle status field (intake/analyzed/analysis_failed/completed) with an explicit transition map enforcing controlled status changes (illegal moves such as completed->intake are rejected; same-status calls are idempotent no-ops), a PATCH /requests/<id>/status endpoint for updates, a GET /requests/<id> endpoint returning current status plus the full chronological audit trail, and durable SQLite-backed audit entries for every status change.

criteria.text: Given an unclear requirement, when it is detected, then the system generates follow-up questions.
Given a complete requirement, when it is reviewed, then no follow-up questions are generated.
Trust: The system logs all clarification interactions in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Adds deterministic missing-field detection (src/requirement_clarification.py) over the seven fields analyze_email()/analyze_report() already extract, a POST /requests/<id>/clarify endpoint that returns one follow-up question per missing field (empty list when complete), and an audit entry for every clarification call via a new RequestIntake.record_clarification(). Split the audit log out of request_intake.py into src/audit_trail.py because request_intake.py was already over this repo's 200-line file cap before this change. Also fixed a pre-existing key mismatch in src/excel_analysis.py ('objectives' vs 'business_objectives') that would have broken clarification for Excel-sourced requests.

criteria.text: Given an Excel report, when it is uploaded, then the system maps fields to approved tables.
Given a field with no mapping, when it is processed, then the system flags it for review.
Trust: The system logs all mapping actions in the audit trail.

stories.notes: Maps uploaded report headers (.xlsx/.xlsm via openpyxl, plus .csv) to this repo's one existing approved schema -- REQUIRED_FIELDS from src/email_analysis.py (business_objectives, scope, kpis, filters, calculations, visual_requirements, reporting_expectations), the same fields excel_analysis.py and requirement_clarification.py already validate against; no richer table/column schema exists yet (that's STORY-005+). Unmatched headers are returned in a 'flagged' list rather than silently dropped, unlike excel_analysis.py's own header scan. New POST /requests/field-mapping endpoint follows the submit_excel_request() pattern (reject bad extension before creating a request; mark analysis_failed-style only for a corrupt/empty file after creation). Routes live in a new src/field_mapping_routes.py rather than inline in app.py, which was already at 197 of this repo's 200-line cap (same reason STORY-003 split audit_trail.py out of request_intake.py). Extended RequestIntake.record_clarification() with an optional error_category param (default None, existing callers/tests unchanged) and reused it as-is for field-mapping audit events rather than adding a near-duplicate method, since request_intake.py had only ~17 lines of headroom left. openpyxl was already in requirements.txt from STORY-001. Also includes a `python -m src.field_mapping <path>` CLI entry point for running the mapping directly without the Flask server. Also has a separate, disconnected prototype in docs/Assignment_1/scripts/field_mapping.py from earlier in this session (against an unrelated made-up KB schema) -- superseded by this src/ implementation and not part of this verification.
